## Mothur v1.48.3 and SILVA v138.2 and clustering into groups of three for the stats

```{r}
library(decontam)
library(ggplot2)
library(vegan)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)
library(grid)
library(reshape2)
library(phyloseq)
library(Polychrome)
library(tidyverse)
library(viridis)
library(emmeans)
library(ggpubr)
```

```{r}
setwd("D:/TEGU_CODE_FILE_MASTER") #working directory 

theme_set(theme_bw())

source("miseqR.R")
# this file is saved in the working directory
```

## Data Import

Now I will import all of the mothur data along with the updated metadata file:

```{r}
# Assign variables for imported data
sharedfile = "tegu16s2.shared"
taxfile = "tegu16s2.taxonomy"
mapfile = "Tegu_FinalMetadata.csv"

# Import mothur data
mothur_16s2 <- import_mothur(mothur_shared_file = sharedfile,
  mothur_constaxonomy_file = taxfile)

# Import sample metadata
map <- read.csv(mapfile)
```

Convert the metadata dataframe into phyloseq format with a simple constructor. The only formatting required to merge the sample data into a phyloseq object is that the row names must match the sample names in your shared and taxonomy files.

```{r}
map <- sample_data(map)

# Assign rownames to be Sample names 
rownames(map) <- map$SampleName

# Merge mothurdata object with sample metadata
Bact_merge <- merge_phyloseq(mothur_16s2, map)
Bact_merge
```

```{r}
colnames(tax_table(Bact_merge)) #these names are not helpful

#change column names 
colnames(tax_table(Bact_merge)) <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", 
  "Order", "Family", "Genus")
```

## Decontam

Using the decontam package to remove any contamination that was introduced during the extraction and PCR process. Lets look at the library size:

```{r}
df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(Bact_merge)) # Put sample_data into a ggplot-friendly data.frame
df$LibrarySize <- sample_sums(Bact_merge)
df <- df[order(df$LibrarySize),]
df$Index <- seq(nrow(df))
ggplot(data=df, aes(x=Index, y=LibrarySize, color=SampleORControl)) + geom_point()
```

The primary true samples fall within 10,000-40,000 reads, with fewer reads in the control. However, I started with three controls (2 extraction blanks and a PCR Blank). One of the extractions blanks and the PCR blanks initially had low read counts and were poorly sequenced. These resulted on getting trimmed completely from the data set, so we are working with one blank alone.

I am going to examine the frequency method to remove contaminants. The frequency method uses the distribution frequency of of each sequence feature as a function of the DNA input and the prevalence method compares presence and absence between the controls and true samples. Lets look at them separately.

```{r}
#frequency default threshold 0.1 
contamdf.freq <- isContaminant(Bact_merge, method="frequency", conc="DNAQuant")
head(contamdf.freq)
```

We can see whether or not a sequence statistically deviates from the set threshold looking at the \$contaminant column.

```{r}
table(contamdf.freq$contaminant)
```

Out of the total 34,610 sequences, 168 have been identified as potential contaminants.

```{r}
bact.noncontam <- prune_taxa(!contamdf.freq$contaminant, Bact_merge)
bact.noncontam
```

We now have 34,442 sequences to work with.

## Graphical Analyses

#### Sample Summary:

Looking at the distribution of the read counts from the samples, this is very similar to what we did earlier before we performed our decontam:

```{r}
summary_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(bact.noncontam)) #create a new data frame 
summary_df$LibrarySize <- sample_sums(bact.noncontam)
summary_df <- summary_df[order(summary_df$LibrarySize),]
summary_df$Index <- seq(nrow(summary_df))

png("LibrarySizeTegu16s.png", width = 800, height = 600)
ggplot(data=summary_df, aes(x=Index, y=LibrarySize, color=Location)) + geom_point()
dev.off()
```

We see that the swabs have the lowest read counts and that the controls and tegu soils are similar to each other in read counts.

```{r}
#min, max, and mean of the sample read counts 
smin <- min(sample_sums(bact.noncontam))
smean <- mean(sample_sums(bact.noncontam))
smax <- max(sample_sums(bact.noncontam))
total_dataset_reads <- sum(sample_sums(bact.noncontam))
```

The minimum read count is 2 sequences, the maximum is 459,532 and the mean is \~168,089

#### Stacked Barplots:

Reduce the phyla to remove the less than 2% reads.

```{r}
teg16s_phylum2 <- bact.noncontam %>%
  tax_glom(taxrank = "Phylum") %>%  
  transform_sample_counts(function(x) {x/sum(x)} ) %>%  
  psmelt() %>% 
   filter(Abundance > 0.02) %>%    # Filter out low abundance taxa
  arrange(Phylum)
```

```{r}
#filtering into treatment groups

BCon <-filter(teg16s_phylum2,Location == "Control")
BDecomp <-filter(teg16s_phylum2,Location == "Tegu")
BSwab<- filter(teg16s_phylum2,Location == "Swab")
```

```{r}
levels(teg16s_phylum2$Phylum)
```

And now lets do Genus:

```{r}
teg16s_genus <- bact.noncontam %>%
```

Too much data to include, but there was an increased relative abundance of the fly associated Ignatzschineria in the swabs in the active decomposition, which is associated with flies that did not show up in soils. Also Oblitimonas found in more advanced stages, might break down carbohydrates. Let us pull these genera out.

```{r}
relabun.genus.16s <- transform_sample_counts(bact.noncontam,function(x) x / sum(x))
bact_genus <- tax_glom(relabun.genus.16s, taxrank = "Genus", NArm = FALSE)
genus_sub_16s <- subset_taxa(bact_genus, Genus %in% c("Ignatzschineria", "Oblitimonas"))
genus_16s.df <- psmelt(genus_sub_16s)
head(genus_16s.df)
```

```{r}
Bact_Genus_Summary_16S <- genus_16s.df %>%
  group_by(Location, Stage, Genus) %>%
  summarize(mean_abund = mean(Abundance, na.rm=TRUE)) 
head(Bact_Genus_Summary_16S)

ConGenus <-filter(Bact_Genus_Summary_16S,Location == "Control")
DecompGenus <-filter(Bact_Genus_Summary_16S,Location == "Tegu")
SwabGenus <- filter(Bact_Genus_Summary_16S,Location == "Swab")
Ignatz <- filter(Bact_Genus_Summary_16S,Genus == "Ignatzschineria")
Oblit <- filter(Bact_Genus_Summary_16S,Genus == "Oblitimonas")
```

```{r}
Ignatz <- subset(Ignatz, Location != 'Blank ')
Ignatz.mod <- aov(mean_abund~factor(Location)+Error(factor(Stage)), data = Ignatz)
summary(Ignatz.mod)  
#There is a  significant difference depending on location (p=0.0161)
#do a post hoc  
Ignatz.emm <- emmeans(Ignatz.mod, ~ Location)
pairs(Ignatz.emm)
#significant difference between control and swab (p=0.03) and swab and tegu (p=0.031) but not control and tegu 
```

```{r}
Oblit <- subset(Oblit, Location != 'Blank ')
Oblit.mod <- aov(mean_abund~factor(Location)+Error(factor(Stage)), data = Oblit)
summary(Oblit.mod)  
#There is a  significant difference depending on location (p=0.00307)
#do a post hoc
Oblit.emm <- emmeans(Oblit.mod, ~ Location)
pairs(Oblit.emm)
#significant difference between control and swab (p=0.007) and swab and tegu (p=0.0074) but not control and tegu 
```

#### Ordination (Unconstrained):

Lets try a PCoA:

```{r}
all16s <- subset_samples(bact.noncontam, Stage != 'Void ') #this will have everything sans the blank and removed sample 

all16_scale <- all16s %>%
  scale_reads(round = "round") #this is from the miseqR.R file

#comparing sample types from different decomposition stages
sample_data(all16_scale)$Stage <- factor(
  sample_data(all16_scale)$Stage, 
  levels = c("Early", "Bloat", "Active I", "Active II", "Active III ", "Advanced I", "Advanced II", "Advanced III", "Skeletal I ", "Skeletal II"))

#ordinnate the data 
all16_pcoa <- ordinate(
  physeq = all16_scale, 
 method = "PCoA", 
  distance = "bray"
)
```

```{r}
#This is exploratory to see if there is any clusering of sample types 
plot_ordination(
  physeq = all16_scale,
  ordination = all16_pcoa,
  shape = "Location",
  color = "Stage",
  title = "PCoA of Bacterial Communities") + 
  labs(shape = "Location") +
  scale_color_viridis(discrete = TRUE, option = "C")+
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Stage), 
             alpha = 0.7, 
             size = 5) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey90", 
             size = 1.5)+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12), axis.title.x = element_text(size=14), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14), plot.title = element_text(size = 20))
```

Distinct clustering with the soils more similar to each other than they are to the swabs, but the two soil types are still different.

Now I want to just subset the soil:

```{r}
soilbact <- subset_samples(bact.noncontam, Source == 'Soil ')
soilbact2 <- subset_samples(soilbact, Stage != 'Void ')
#scale to even read depth 
soil16_scale <- soilbact2 %>%
  scale_reads(round = "round") #this is from the miseqR.R file

#comparing sample types from different decomposition stages
sample_data(soil16_scale)$Stage <- factor(
  sample_data(soil16_scale)$Stage, 
  levels = c("Early", "Bloat", "Active I", "Active II", "Active III ", "Advanced I", "Advanced II", "Advanced III", "Skeletal I ", "Skeletal II"))

#ordinnate the data 
soil16_pcoa <- ordinate(
  physeq = soil16_scale, 
 method = "PCoA", 
  distance = "bray"
)
```

Now do biplot with the chemical data overlaying:

```{r}
# Create the distance matrix
soil16_dist <-phyloseq::distance(physeq = soil16_scale, method = "bray")

# Create the CAP ordination
soil16_cap_ord <- ordinate(
  physeq = soil16_scale,
  method = "CAP",
  distance = soil16_dist,
  formula = ~ pH + EC + NH4 + NO3 + C + N + CtoN)

pdf("CAPTEGU16sPoster.pdf", width=9, height=6, useDingbats=FALSE)
soil16cap_plot <- plot_ordination(
  physeq = soil16_scale, 
  ordination = soil16_cap_ord,
  color = "Stage",
  shape = "Location"
  ) + 
    theme_classic() +
   labs(shape = 'Treatment') +
  scale_color_viridis(discrete = TRUE, option = "C")+
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Stage), alpha = 0.7, size = 6) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("Tegu" = 15, "Control" = 16)) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 18), axis.title.x = element_text(size=20), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 18),axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20), plot.title = element_text(size = 24)) 
  
# add metadata as arrows
Soil16_arrows <- vegan::scores(soil16_cap_ord, display = "bp")

#add labels and create dataframe
Soil16_arrows_df <- data.frame(labels = rownames(Soil16_arrows), Soil16_arrows)

# create arrow aesthetics
ar_aesthetics <- aes(xend = CAP1, yend = CAP2, x = 0, y = 0, shape = NULL, color = NULL, label = labels)
lb_aesthetics <- aes (x = 1.2 * CAP1, y = 1.5 * CAP2, shape = NULL, color = NULL, label = labels)
ar_head = arrow(length = unit (0.02, "npc"))

# overlay arrows
soil16cap_plot+
  geom_segment(mapping = ar_aesthetics, size = 1.25, data = Soil16_arrows_df, color = "black", arrow = ar_head) + 
  geom_label(mapping = lb_aesthetics, size = 4, data = Soil16_arrows_df, color= "black", show.legend = FALSE)
dev.off()
```

Then lets look at each sample type in respect to stage of decomposition.

```{r}
decomp_bact <- subset_samples(bact.noncontam, Location == 'Tegu')
decomp_bact2 <- subset_samples(decomp_bact, Stage != 'Void ')

decomp16_scale <- decomp_bact2 %>%
  scale_reads(round = "round") #this is from the miseqR.R file

#comparing sample types from different decomposition stages
sample_data(decomp16_scale)$Stage <- factor(
```

#### **PERMANOVA:**

Testing the hypothesis that the three different sample locations (Control soils, Tegu decomp soils, and skin swabs) have different centroids.

```{r}
set.seed(3)

# Calculate bray curtis distance matrix with all_scale because it has all samples sans the blank 
all16_bray <- phyloseq::distance(all16_scale, method = "bray") 

# make a data frame from the sample_data and have to use all which is the data with blank removed
all16df <- data.frame(sample_data(all16s))

# Adonis test
adonis(all16_bray ~ Location, data = all16df)

# Homogeneity of dispersion test
beta16_all <- betadisper(all16_bray, all16df$Location)
permutest(beta16_all)
```

It looks like there is a differences in community centroids based on sampling location. However, I want to do this for just the soil as well.

```{r}
set.seed(3)

# Calculate bray curtis distance matrix with soil_scale because it has only the soil samples
soil16_bray <- phyloseq::distance(soil16_scale, method = "bray") 

# make a data frame from the sample_data and have to use which is the data with just soils 
soil16df <- data.frame(sample_data(soilbact2))

# Adonis test
adonis(soil16_bray ~ Location, data = soil16df)

# Homogeneity of dispersion test
beta16soil <- betadisper(soil16_bray, soil16df$Location)
permutest(beta16soil)
```

And there is still a significant difference in between the soil communities.

#### Alpha Diversity:

First, I must perform rarefaction, although rarefaction has its issues, this needs to be done for these metrics.

```{r}
min_lib <- min(sample_sums(all16s))

#the minimum library is 74 with all samples, which is too small 

min_lib2 <- min(sample_sums(soilbact2))

#if we don't include the swabs, this makes it so the min library size is 26,318 

#I also want to seperate out just the swabs 
skinbact <- subset_samples(bact.noncontam, Source == 'Skin')
skinbact2 <- subset_samples(skinbact, Stage != 'Void ')

min_lib3 <- min(sample_sums(skinbact2))
#same as min library one, 74, which means the soils and swabs must be processed seperately
```

Making arefaction curves:

```{r}
#to make the rarefaction curve, need to extract otu table 
taxa_are_rows(bact.noncontam)

OTUtab16s <- otu_table(bact.noncontam) 
class(OTUtab16s) <- "matrix" # as.matrix() will do nothing
## you get a warning here, but this is what we need to have
OTUtab16s <- t(OTUtab16s) # transpose observations to row
```

```{r}
#rareify 
rare16S <- rarecurve(OTUtab16s, step = 100)
```

```{r}
#piping data from rarecurve into ggplot 
map_dfr(rare16S, bind_rows) %>%
  bind_cols(SampleID = rownames(OTUtab16s),.) %>%
  pivot_longer(-SampleID) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(n_seqs = as.numeric(str_replace(name, "N", ""))) %>%
  select(-name) %>%
 ggplot(aes(x=n_seqs, y=value, group=SampleID, color=SampleID)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept=min_lib, color="gray") +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x="Sample Size", y="Species") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") 
ggsave("Original16SRarePlot.pdf", width=8, height=5)
```

As we can see, this needs to be redone with the soil and the skin swab libraries separate. Time to rarefy soil samples:

```{r}
#to make the rarefaction curve, need to extract otu table 
taxa_are_rows(soilbact2)
soil16stab <- otu_table(soilbact2)
class(soil16stab) <- "matrix" # as.matrix() will do nothing
## you get a warning here, but this is what we need to have
soil16stab <- t(soil16stab) # transpose observations to rows
```

```{r}
soil16srare <- rarecurve(soil16stab, step = 100)
```

```{r}
#piping data from rarecurve into ggplot 
map_dfr(soil16srare, bind_rows) %>%
  bind_cols(SampleID = rownames(soil16stab),.) %>%
  pivot_longer(-SampleID) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(n_seqs = as.numeric(str_replace(name, "N", ""))) %>%
  select(-name) %>%
 ggplot(aes(x=n_seqs, y=value, group=SampleID, color=SampleID)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept=min_lib2, color="gray") +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x="Sample Size", y="Species") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") 
ggsave("raresoil16plot.pdf", width=8, height=5)
```

```{r}
# Initialize matrices to store richness and evenness estimates for all of the samples for statistical analysis and visualization 
soil16bact <- subset_samples(soilbact, Stage != 'Void ')


nsoilsamp = nsamples(soil16bact)
soiltrials = 100

soilrichness <- matrix(nrow = nsoilsamp, ncol = soiltrials)
row.names(soilrichness) <- sample_names(soil16bact)

soilevenness <- matrix(nrow = nsoilsamp, ncol = soiltrials)
row.names(soilevenness) <- sample_names(soil16bact)

soilshanmeas <- matrix(nrow = nsoilsamp, ncol = soiltrials)
row.names(soilshanmeas) <- sample_names(soil16bact)

# It is always important to set a seed when you subsample so your result is replicable 
set.seed(4)

for (i in 1:100) {
  # Subsample
  rs <- rarefy_even_depth(soil16bact, sample.size = min_lib2, verbose = FALSE, replace = TRUE)
  
  # Calculate richness
  richsoil <- as.numeric(as.matrix(estimate_richness(rs, measures = "Observed")))
  soilrichness[ ,i] <- richsoil
  
  # Calculate evenness
  evensoil <- as.numeric(as.matrix(estimate_richness(rs, measures = "InvSimpson")))
  soilevenness[ ,i] <- evensoil

  #calc Shannon
  Shannonsoil <- as.numeric(as.matrix(estimate_richness(rs, measures = "Shannon")))
  soilshanmeas[ ,i] <- Shannonsoil
}

# Create a new dataframe to hold the means and standard deviations of richness estimates
SampleID <- row.names(soilrichness)
mean <- apply(soilrichness, 1, mean)
sd <- apply(soilrichness, 1, sd)
measure <- rep("Richness", nsoilsamp)
rich_stats_soil <- data.frame(SampleID, mean, sd, measure)

# Create a new dataframe to hold the means and standard deviations of evenness estimates
SampleID <- row.names(soilevenness)
mean <- apply(soilevenness, 1, mean)
sd <- apply(soilevenness, 1, sd)
measure <- rep("Inverse Simpson", nsoilsamp)
even_stats_soil <- data.frame(SampleID, mean, sd, measure)

# Create a new dataframe to hold the means and standard deviations of evenness estimates
SampleID <- row.names(soilshanmeas)
mean <- apply(soilshanmeas, 1, mean)
sd <- apply(soilshanmeas, 1, sd)
measure <- rep("Shannon", nsoilsamp)
shan_stats_soil <- data.frame(SampleID, mean, sd, measure)
```

```{r}
#Now we will combine our estimates for soil richness and evenness into one dataframe

soilalpha <- rbind(rich_stats_soil, even_stats_soil, shan_stats_soil)

#add metadata 

j <- data.frame(sample_data(soil16bact))
colnames(j)[2] <- "SampleID"
adivsoil <- merge(soilalpha, j, by = "SampleID")
```

```{r}
#filter out the data for this test 

ObRichSl <-filter(adivsoil,measure == "Richness")
ShannonSl <-filter(adivsoil,measure == "Shannon")
InvSimpSl <- filter(adivsoil,measure == "Inverse Simpson")
```

```{r}
theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust=1, size = 14), axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16))
```
